```yaml
name: Sign-and-attest
``` 

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of simple security defaults in Kubernetes and CI gates that prevent risky deployments.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics: default-deny, ingress/egress rules
- CI gate that scans manifests across namespaces
- Local + CI validation workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/netpol-gate.yml
name: NetPol Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  netpol-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - run: kubectl version --client
      - run: |
          for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
            kubectl -n $ns get networkpolicy >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing NP in $ns"; exit 1; }
          done
```

```yaml
# examples/fail/no-netpol.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
```

```yaml
# examples/pass/default-deny.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

```yaml
# Kyverno policy skeleton
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-digest-private-registry
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: digest-required
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "DaemonSet", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Images must reference a digest and use private registry with imagePullSecrets."
      pattern:
        spec.template.spec.containers[].image: '*@sha256:*'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a scalable, automated policy gate across multi-cloud clusters using Gatekeeper/OPA, Cosign attestations, and runtime security constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Cosign attestation and image provenance
- Registry allowlist and image provenance checks
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop capabilities
- CI integration and gatekeeper audit verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (Gatekeeper) minimal sketch
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecuredcontainers
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecuredContainers
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8ssecuredcontainers
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not signed(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Container image %v must be cosign-signed", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not allowed_registry(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Registry %v not in allowlist", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
          msg := "Container must run as non-root"
        }
```

## What to Look For

- Demonstrates understanding of OPA/Gatekeeper policy structure
- Shows proper cosign attestation validation approach
- Includes comprehensive runtime security constraints
- Outlines practical CI/CD integration strategy

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
 - Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
 - ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
 - Pod security hardening
 - Kubernetes admission webhook behavior

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate example (high level)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata: {name: K8sContainerHardening}
# ...
```
```yaml
# Constraint example
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sContainerHardeningConstraint
metadata: {name: harden-containers}
spec:
  match: { kinds: [{ apiGroups: [""], kinds: ["Pod"] }] }
  parameters:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml

apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1

metadata:

    kinds:

      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
```
